Billing/procurement: procurement@bluerocklabs.com is on copy for any required PO. If there's a short form or contract we should sign, point us to it.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of AI, BlueRock Labs

I pulled the customer-facing record and attached a quick CSV export of trial activity. High-level notes:
- Domain: bluerocklabs.com has three active eval accounts matching the addresses Sarah listed.
- Two of the accounts requested additional credits within a 48-hour window last month and were granted small extensions (15k/20k).
- There's a pattern of short bursts followed by account rotation (different usernames, same billing email domain).
- No previous enterprise contract on file; last touch was a demo in Nov 2027.

I've attached trial-log-20280209.csv. My recommendation: escalate to fraud analysis before approving further credits; if we move forward, require a PO and limit to one controlled pilot account.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial-log-20280209.csv (trial activity export)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 14:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary eval credit bump for multiple teams

Folks — ran the signals and here's a concise summary (see attached notes):
- IP/geo: two of the three accounts show overlapping source IP ranges during the initial signup window (same cloud provider ASN), which is suspicious for coordinated evals.
- Promo history: multiple small credit grants in Q4 2027 and Jan 2028; timestamps show parallel requests originating within hours of each other.
- Device/billing fuzz: browser fingerprints vary but billing metadata (payment token suffixes, where applicable) shows reuse patterns consistent with shared org-level resources.
- Risk score: medium-high for promo abuse (not outright fraud yet).

Recommendation: deny unconditional free credits. Offer a commercial pilot instead — require a PO or prepayment for a 30-day pilot with a capped token allotment (e.g., 50k tokens) and a clause that we will terminate extensions if pattern continues. If Sales wants to support momentum, approve a single pilot account for one team only after PO is received.

--
Priyom Das
Fraud & Risk Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fraud-analysis-notes-20280211.txt

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 08:29:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary eval credit bump for multiple teams

Appreciate the thorough analysis. Customer context to consider: Sarah is pushing fast because their exec sponsor is evaluating vendor choices this month — losing momentum risks moving them to a competitor. They asked specifically for parallel test lanes because their teams operate independently and want equivalent baselines.

I propose a compromise that aligns with Priyom's recommendation: offer a single paid pilot (50k tokens) for one canonical team (engineering@bluerocklabs.com) on a 30-day PO, and provide a one-time 25k token trial credit on the second account after we receive the PO and a short success checklist at 14 days. No unconditional mass grants. This keeps guardrails but preserves momentum.

If leadership signs off, I'll email Sarah with the offer and draft the commercial terms.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary eval credit bump for multiple teams

Thanks everyone — aligned decision and playbook: 
1) No blanket grants. Do not increase credits for all three accounts.
2) Offer a single commercial pilot (50k tokens) for engineering@bluerocklabs.com, contingent on a PO or prepayment and an agreed success checklist.
3) Offer a one-time, conditional 25k eval credit to a second account only after PO is received and initial 14-day milestone is met.
4) Require procurement@bluerocklabs.com to sign the PO and include billing details; Legal to review only if the customer requests non-standard terms.
5) Ben — please send the counter-offer as a single email to Sarah + procurement, copy Marissa. Include links to our pilot quote (DocuSign) and attach the trial activity export and fraud notes for transparency.
6) Priyom — add the customer to watchlist for 90 days; flag for further promo gating if the pattern repeats.

I'll draft a short internal note to leadership for visibility.

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
